text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: streaming-prod-us-east-1 p99 decode latency > 2.5s for last 10m on /v1/stream (alerts: p99>2s, p95>600ms). Auto-escalate to oncall. Runbook: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/streaming-decode
lauren: oncall here, picking up. seeing alerts in dashboard, correlated with a deploy ~12:10 UTC. starting triage.
matt: confirmed. rolling p95 jumped at 12:11, p99 spike coincides with increased tail responses and streaming stalls. Logs show repeated "kv-cache-evict" and "cuda-kernel-alloc-failure" on a subset of nodes.
jia: 12:08 deploy rolled kernel+trt8 libs to k8s node-pool-a. That's suspicious. I pushed a small compiler-flag tweak earlier today (-ftls-fast) which landed in that build.
darren: grabbing logs from affected pods now. fetching decoder traces. Using `kubectl -n streaming logs -l pool=node-pool-a --since=15m`.
devx-bot: deploy-bot: Deployment "inference-runtime-v2.3.4" completed at 2026-03-15T12:07:54Z on node-pool-a (image: redwood/inference:v2.3.4-kernelp).
lauren: priority: mitigate customer impact first. Can we divert traffic to node-pool-b (older stable kernel) as hot fallback?
matt: yes we can. I can update routing policy in 2m to route new sessions to pool-b and let existing streams drain. Will create canary rule: prefer pool-b for new connections.
jia: note: the new kernel changed a kernel compile path that alters flashattn kernel selection; it seems to pick a new codepath that has poor eviction behavior under streaming KV pressure.
darren: tail traces attached: ```
[trace] decode frame 0..512: kernel launch ok
[trace] decode frame 513..1024: KV cache miss -> allocate tmp -> cudaMalloc failed intermittently -> fallback path triggers heavy memcpy -> stall ~1.2s
```
lauren: that matches customer reports of intermittent stalls. Customer support pinged CUST-4822, waiting update.
customer-success: converting to incident. Several customers in region reported timeouts, one enterprise customer saw 8% error increase on streaming calls. We're preparing an outbound.
matt: mitigation plan: 1) reroute new sessions to pool-b (in progress) 2) disable the new compile flag by rolling back runtime image on pool-a or patch config to force old kernel selection. Which is faster?
jia: forcing old kernel selection via env `FORCE_KERNEL_VARIANT=legacy` is fast and non-disruptive; it forces the runtime to pick the stable flashattn codepath. Patch and rollout to pool-a should be under 5m.
darren: I'm patching the daemonset on pool-a: `kubectl -n streaming set env ds/inference-runtime FORCE_KERNEL_VARIANT=legacy --record` and then `kubectl rollout restart ds/inference-runtime -l pool=node-pool-a`. Starting now.
ops-bot: action taken: routing-change initiated by matt, devx-bot, and environment patch requested.
devx-bot: router: traffic policy updated — new-session weight: pool-b 100% (old sessions draining on pool-a).
lauren: observing metrics after reroute. p95 dropping slowly, p99 still elevated on draining nodes. Keep an eye on error budget.
sre-bot: FYI: autoscaler on pool-b is at 70% capacity, might need temporary burst capacity for traffic shift. Recommend enabling burst nodes for 10m.
matt: enabling burst. `gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize --size +5 ...` (done). New capacity coming up.
darren: rollout restart completed on affected pods with env set. Pod logs show runtime selecting legacy kernel now. Sample log: `kernel-selector: forcing legacy flashattn path (env FORCE_KERNEL_VARIANT=legacy)`.
lauren: telemetry at 12:21: p95 420ms, p99 1.1s (was 2.6s). Errors decreased to ~1.2% above baseline (was 8%). Good progress.
jia: I'll open a revert PR for the compile-flag change and mark the kernel variant change as blocked until we root-cause. We need a reproduction harness for streaming workload reproducer under KV pressure.
matt: agree. Immediate next steps: keep reroute for another 20m, let pool-a drain, monitor p99 and customer queues. If stable, we can mark incident mitigated and follow up with postmortem.
customer-success: sending interim customer notice: "We've mitigated a streaming latency issue in us-east-1 by routing traffic away from impacted hosts and applying a runtime fallback. We're monitoring and will follow up with a timeline."
lauren: can someone own the post-incident forensics? Need to correlate allocator behavior, kernel selection heuristics, and TRT flashattn changes. Jia, you ok to lead with Matt for infra traces?
jia: I can lead. Will collect nvprof-like traces, kernel launch profiles, and compile flags. Matt will help with operator-level logs and routing artifacts.
darren: I'll snapshot affected nodes (/var/log/nvidia, dmesg) and upload to shared incident folder: https://redwood.incidents/7743219000. Also I'll preserve pod images for debugging.
lauren: timeframe: incident declared at 12:10, mitigated to 'reduced customer impact' at 12:21, keep channel open for 60m for monitoring. If p99 <1s and errors near baseline for 30m, we'll mark resolved and start postmortem.
ops-bot: Incident status update: Mitigation applied (12:21 UTC) — traffic rerouted, runtime forced to legacy kernel on pool-a. Monitoring for stabilization.
matt: handoff note for next oncall: if p99 climbs after draining completes, escalate to "kernel-build" and consider rolling back to previous image entirely. Document: https://redwood/internal/playbooks/kernel-rollbacks
lauren: thanks all. Good rapid response. Leaving channel but will be reachable.
jia: collecting artifacts now, will attach reproducer and proposed test matrix to PM.
darren: uploading logs + node snapshots (links in folder).
customer-success: will update customers once we confirm 30m stable.
lauren: closing loop: last check 12:54 — p95=360ms p99=860ms errors ~0.3% above baseline, continuing observation. If stable at 13:20, convert to postmortem.
ops-bot: Incident channel will remain read-only after resolution, please move follow-ups to #postmortems once incident is closed.
